object_description: two new volumes framing elevated school spaces
design_condition: Two new volumes are composed with existing buildings to form differentiated outdoor spaces, including a neighborhood-facing playground and an elevated school square connected to the landscape.

positive.statement: The placement of two new volumes creates a balanced spatial composition with the existing buildings.
The arrangement creates differentiated and meaningful outdoor spaces with high quality of stay.
The school square is well connected to the neighborhood and school use and is suitable for larger events.
The low building provides very good orientation for small children.
The basic-level arrangement with direct stairs and assigned atria is attractive and guarantees direct access to outdoor space.
The access and escape-route concept allows flexible use and supports a wide variety of teaching concepts.
The continuous central room can be ideally used for larger projects and different forms of learning.
The pleasant proportions and plausible facade treatment are convincing.
The design responds appropriately and cleverly to the location and complex task.

negative.statement: The bicycle and container parking spaces are topographically and unfavorably positioned at the point of access.
The colonnade has good recreational qualities but could be a little wider.
The day-school arrangement is schematic and needs revision to accommodate different age groups.
The entrance qualities are not convincing because of the somewhat hidden, narrow stairs.
The floor is too densely organized, while the number of students requires more space to move around.
A more central location for the school management would improve accessibility for external visitors.
The facades remain too neutral and fall short of the qualities of the floor plans.
The buildings need more sophistication and a targeted use of exceptions at entrances and corners.
The primary school has rather dark sections of space toward the middle zone.
The skeleton building is rather complex in terms of gray energy and greenhouse gas emissions.
